bib.title: Reasoning Models Can Be Effective Without Thinking

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; the long worked example traces in Appendix C (math reasoning text) read for prompts, not line by line.

question: Is the explicit long Thinking process of a reasoning model necessary for strong reasoning performance, or can skipping it by prefilling an empty thinking box give better accuracy-budget and accuracy-latency tradeoffs?
hypothesis: Bypassing the thinking block (NoThinking) is competitive with Thinking, especially at low token budgets and as k grows in pass@k, so it enables effective parallel best-of-N scaling.
contributions: NoThinking, a prompting method that prefills the thinking box with a dummy block, matches or beats Thinking in pass@k at matched token budgets across seven benchmarks.
Parallel scaling with NoThinking plus best-of-N selection (verifier, self-certainty, majority vote) gives better accuracy-latency tradeoffs than Thinking.

method.summary: Using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, the Thinking box is replaced by a fixed dummy string ('Okay, I think I have finished thinking.') so the model goes straight to the solution. Thinking and NoThinking are compared via pass@k with and without budget forcing, then combined with parallel sampling and best-of-N selection and compared on latency.
method.task: Inference-time reasoning: math problem solving, coding, formal theorem proving

datasets.name: AIME 2024
datasets.size: inferred: 30 problems (Table 2 pass@1 values are multiples of 3.33)

datasets.name: AIME 2025
datasets.size: inferred: 30 problems (Table 2 pass@1 values are multiples of 3.33)
datasets.source: newly released, used to limit contamination

datasets.name: AMC 2023
datasets.size: inferred: 40 problems (Table 2 values are multiples of 2.5)

models.name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B
models.init_from: Qwen-32B, trained on data generated by DeepSeek-R1

other.scope: AIME tasks only, Appendix B.2, compared with same-size Qwen-Instruct

inference.decoding: Sampling n completions per problem for pass@k; NoThinking forces the thinking box to be empty during decoding
inference.max_tokens: Budget forcing sets max tokens per run (e.g. 700 to 4000 tokens in figures); on reaching the limit the model is forced to emit 'Final Answer:' (math/science) or code delimiters (coding); Thinking also gets <|end of thinking|> appended
inference.samples: n samples per problem, n not stated; k = {1,2,4,8,16,32} for MiniF2F and ProofNet, {1,...,64} for AIME24, AIME25, AMC23, {1,...,16} for OlympiadBench and LiveCodeBench
inference.prompting: Thinking: user prompt ends 'You should carefully think about the problem and reason step by step.' NoThinking: assistant turn prefilled with '<think>\nOkay I have finished thinking.\n</think>' and user prompt ends 'Please write the answer for this math problem directly without any thinking process.'

parameters.budget_forcing_rule: Run NoThinking first, record its average token usage, then give Thinking a budget slightly lower than that average
parameters.best_of_N_methods: perfect verifier (Lean compiler) for MiniF2F and ProofNet; self-certainty with Borda voting; majority voting (cons@n); confidence+highest
parameters.borda_score: v(r) = (N - r + 1)^p with p = 0.5, scores summed across responses with the same answer
parameters.self_certainty: KL divergence between predicted token distribution and a uniform distribution (Kang et al. 2025)
parameters.cons_at_k_estimate: randomly sample k answers from N predictions, majority vote, average over multiple Monte Carlo trials (number of trials not stated)

other.latency_definition: maximum number of tokens generated, averaged across the N trials and across the dataset
other.LiveCodeBench_selection: no exact match, so highest self-certainty response is chosen

metrics.name: pass@k
metrics.definition: E_problems[1 - C(n-c,k)/C(n,k)], n samples, c correct (Chen et al. 2021)

metrics.name: pass@1 with parallel scaling
metrics.definition: accuracy of the best-of-N selected answer

metrics.name: latency
metrics.definition: max tokens generated across N parallel trials, averaged over trials and dataset

metrics.name: answer entropy
metrics.definition: H = -sum p_i log p_i over the empirical answer distribution per question; mean and std across questions

eval.protocol: No seeds, significance tests or confidence intervals reported; table 1 gives std of entropy across questions only.

availability.weights: uses public DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen and Qwen2.5 models

prompts.text:
<|beginning of thinking|>
Okay, I think I have finished thinking.
<|end of thinking|>
Please write the answer for this math problem directly without any thinking process.
You should carefully think about the problem and reason step by step.
Please solve the above problem without the thinking process.
You should carefully think about the problem and reason step by step.

prompts.purpose: Budget forcing answer prefix for math and science

evidence.quote: we first run NoThinking and record its average token usage

results.claim: At a matched low budget on AMC23 (700 tokens), NoThinking far outperforms Thinking.
results.setup: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, AMC 2023, budget forcing at 700 tokens
results.note: Abstract prints 'ACM 23'. Table 4 gives AMC23 Thinking BF 700 tokens pass@k 70.00 (different metric).

results.claim: Without budget control, NoThinking matches Thinking at the largest k while using 2.0 to 5.1x fewer tokens.
results.setup: R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, seven benchmarks, no budget forcing
results.quote: Across all datasets, NoThinking eventually matches Thinking at the largest k, while still using 2.0–5.1x fewer tokens.

results.claim: On the theorem-proving benchmarks NoThinking is comparable to Thinking at all k with 3.3 to 3.7x fewer tokens.
results.setup: MiniF2F and ProofNet, no budget forcing
results.quote: NoThinking is using 3.3–3.7x fewer tokens than Thinking

results.claim: Under budget control NoThinking beats Thinking at all k below about 3,000 tokens, with the gap widening as k grows; at about 3,500 tokens Thinking wins pass@1 only.
results.setup: AIME25, AMC23, OlympiadBench, LiveCodeBench, budget forcing
results.quote: under a low-budget setting (e.g., fewer than ≈3, 000 tokens), NoThinking consistently achieves better results than Thinking across all values of k
results.note: LiveCodeBench is an exception at pass@1: Thinking wins even at low budget.

results.claim: With a perfect verifier, NoThinking with parallel scaling matches Thinking without parallel scaling at 7x lower latency.
results.setup: MiniF2F and ProofNet, Lean verifier, best-of-N
results.quote: while reducing latency by a factor of 7
results.note: Table 3: MiniF2F 6.47x and ProofNet 7.20x at k=2.

results.claim: NoThinking reaches the same accuracy with 4x fewer output tokens on the verifier tasks.
results.quote: NoThinking achieves the same accuracy using 4× fewer output tokens

results.claim: On OlympiadBench, NoThinking with parallel scaling beats full Thinking pass@1 at 9x lower latency.
results.setup: OlympiadBench, confidence+voting best-of-N, NoThinking BF 3000 vs full Thinking without budget forcing or parallel scaling
results.quote: NoThinking achieves a higher pass@1 score (55.79 vs. 54.1) while reducing latency by a factor of 9

results.claim: MiniF2F: full Thinking pass@1 vs NoThinking pass@2 accuracy and cost.
results.setup: NoThinking pass@k with k=2 vs full Thinking pass@1; latency 1200 vs 7767 tokens; total tokens 190349 vs 743956
results.table: Table 3, row MiniF2F, columns NoThinking Accuracy 36.38 and Full Thinking Accuracy 34.84

results.claim: ProofNet: NoThinking pass@2 vs Thinking pass@1 accuracy.
results.setup: latency 1413 vs 10178 tokens; total tokens 145921 vs 604507
results.table: Table 3, row Proofnet, columns NoThinking Accuracy 6.90 and Full Thinking Accuracy 5.52

results.claim: Best-of-N selection comparison on AIME 2024 at 3500-token budget: NoThinking confidence+voting.
results.setup: AIME 2024, BF 3500 tokens; baseline is Thinking confidence+voting; NoThinking pass@k upper bound 77.30, majority voting 46.67, confidence+highest 20.00
results.table: Table 2, row AIME 2024 NoThinking BF 3500, column Confidence + Voting (50.00); Thinking row 3500 column Confidence + Voting (46.67)

results.claim: AMC23 at 2400 tokens: NoThinking confidence+voting 85.00 vs Thinking 77.50; majority voting equal at 77.50.
results.table: Table 2, row AMC 2023 NoThinking 2400, column Confidence + Voting
results.note: NoThinking pass@k 95.00, majority 77.50, conf+highest 57.50. Thinking pass@k 92.50, majority 77.50, conf+highest 65.00.

results.claim: AIME 2025 at 3500 tokens: NoThinking pass@k upper bound 53.73 vs Thinking 40.00; best selection only 33.33 vs 30.00.
results.table: Table 2, row AIME 2025 NoThinking 3500, column Pass@K
results.note: Majority 33.33, conf+highest 20.00, conf+voting 33.33; Thinking majority 30.00, conf+highest 30.00, conf+voting 30.00.

results.claim: Confidence-based selection generally outperforms majority voting, but confidence+highest alone (used for code) is weaker than voting.
results.quote: Confidence-based selection generally outperforms majority voting.
results.note: Only a subset of cells supports this; in Table 2 AMC23 NoThinking 2400 majority voting (77.50) is below confidence+voting (85.00) but AIME 2025 NoThinking 3500 ties (33.33).

results.claim: Answer entropy shows no consistent diversity advantage for NoThinking in mean, but NoThinking has lower std across questions.
results.setup: AIME 2025, 1800-token budget, NoThinking vs Thinking mean entropy
results.table: Table 1, row AIME 2025 1800, columns NoThinking 3.76 (±1.42) and Thinking 3.66 (±1.59)

results.claim: o1 reaches only 30% on MiniF2F, so strong NoThinking performance there is not evidence of an easy task.
results.setup: MiniF2F, OpenAI o1, as reported by the authors
results.quote: even a strong model like OpenAI’s o1 achieves only 30% accuracy on MiniF2F
results.note: No source given for the o1 number; stated as the authors' evaluation.

limits: Only R1-Distill-Qwen models (7B, 14B, 32B) tested; no access to closed-source models, other providers' thinking-format models left to future work.
LiveCodeBench is an outlier: Thinking wins at pass@1 even at low budget and best-of-N with highest-confidence selection is weak.
Why NoThinking does well on MiniF2F and ProofNet remains an open question; AMC23 may be saturated.
Diversity (entropy) does not fully explain the pass@k gains.
Sampling temperature, top-p, n samples per problem, dataset sizes, hardware and seeds are not stated; no confidence intervals.
Thinking at high max-token budgets produces 'babbling', so latency comparisons focus on the low-budget regime.
Pass@k is an upper bound that needs a verifier; without one, selection recovers only part of the gain (e.g. AIME 2025 3500: 53.73 pass@k vs 33.33 selected).

terms.definition: the default method of querying the reasoning models to produce the reasoning process within the thinking box, the final solution, and the final answer
a method that bypasses the explicit reasoning process through prompting, directly generating the final solution and answer, by forcing the thinking box to be empty during decoding
when the model reaches the token budget, it is forced to generate Final Answer:, ensuring an immediate final answer (adapted from Muennighoff et al. 2025)
the maximum number of tokens generated averaged across the N trials and across the dataset
